n: Cross-border mule and payment-chain laundering of fraud proceeds
ds: Proceeds of authorised-push and online fraud are moved rapidly across several mule accounts, payment institutions, correspondent chains and crypto off-ramps in different jurisdictions, so that recall and freezing requests lag behind the funds. Each hop can look unremarkable alone; the signal lies in speed, chain length, data gaps in payment messages and repeated fraud-related recalls. Complements ML-MULE and FR-APP, which focus on single-account and victim-side views.

src.t: FATF, INTERPOL and Egmont Group, Illicit Financial Flows from Cyber-enabled Fraud (2023)
FATF, Recommendation 16 (payment transparency) revisions and Interpretive Note (2025)
FATF, Guidance on Correspondent Banking Services (2016)

cn.rt: Fast onward movement of fraud proceeds through mule everyday and savings accounts into other institutions.

rat: Multi-hop mule chain via PSPs, correspondents and off-ramps.

ind.cx: Cross-border fraud proceeds are forwarded onward within minutes or hours in near-equal amounts, leaving minimal balance at each mule hop.
ind.fp: Legitimate payment intermediaries, treasury sweeps and agents routinely pass funds through quickly.
ind.ds: Funds received into an account are forwarded onward within a very short period, often in near-equal amounts and leaving minimal balance.

ind.n: Rapid movement through correspondent or private banking channels
ind.cx: Large sums transit several banks and jurisdictions after arrival, outpacing recall and freeze requests.
ind.fp: Treasury and liquidity management can cause fast movements.
ind.ds: Large sums move quickly through several banks and jurisdictions after arrival, with no hold period.

ind.n: Missing, incomplete or placeholder originator and beneficiary information
ind.cx: Incoming or outgoing payment messages carry placeholder, truncated or missing originator and beneficiary data, hindering alignment checks and tracing along the chain.
ind.ds: Payment messages omit, truncate or use generic placeholder data for originator or beneficiary details.

ind.n: Sender or intermediary with history of message-quality deficiencies
ind.cx: A particular peer institution or payment provider repeatedly forwards fraud-linked payments with data gaps.
ind.ds: Peer institution frequently sends payments with data gaps.

ind.n: Use of multiple accounts to move funds
ind.cx: Funds are spread across many accounts, wallets and institutions per customer or linked group to fragment the trail and stay under monitoring limits.
ind.ds: Customer spreads activity across many accounts, products or institutions.

ind.n: Rapid sequential conversions across many asset types
ind.cx: At the crypto off-ramp, proceeds are swapped through multiple assets or stablecoins in quick succession before withdrawal to a new platform or wallet.
ind.fp: Active traders, arbitrageurs and market makers.
ind.ds: Funds received are swapped through several tokens or stablecoins in quick succession with no apparent trading rationale before withdrawal.

ind.cx: Assets arriving by cross-chain bridge are sold into fiat or stablecoin and withdrawn quickly, completing the hop from fraud proceeds to cash-out.
ind.ds: Assets arriving via bridge are sold into fiat or stablecoin and withdrawn within a short window.

ind.n: Cross-border corridor with known abuse typologies
ind.cx: Chains repeatedly use corridors and intermediary jurisdictions named in fraud typology reports as common cash-out routes.
ind.fp: Corridors are used mainly by legitimate remittance senders.
ind.ds: Payments use corridors identified in typology reports as high risk, including regions where informal value transfer is prevalent.

ind.n: Repeated fraud recalls or return requests against the same receiving account or originating institution
ind.cx: Several recalls arriving from different foreign institutions against one account is a strong indicator of a cross-border mule hop and justifies immediate restriction and reporting.
ind.fp: Operational errors, duplicate payments, disputed commercial transactions and a single large fraud event hitting one account can generate several recalls without mule activity.
ind.ds: A receiving account, or flows from a given originating institution, attract multiple recall, return or fraud-notification requests in a short period, often followed by funds already having left.

ind.n: Counterparty institution slow or unresponsive to fraud recall and information requests
ind.cx: Weak responsiveness at downstream hops lets proceeds disperse; it informs counterparty risk rating and routing decisions.
ind.fp: Time-zone differences, legal process requirements in the counterparty's jurisdiction and capacity limits can delay legitimate responses.
ind.ds: A correspondent, payment institution or exchange repeatedly fails to act on freeze, recall or request-for-information messages in time, or the same beneficiary institution appears in many fraud cases.

ctl.ds: Model that scores inbound-then-outbound pass-through, new-payee churn, counterparty diversity and profile mismatch to flag likely mule accounts. It prioritises accounts for review and restriction.
Alerts when inflows are quickly moved out with little retained balance, including cash-in fast-out and rapid conversion or cash-out. It reveals accounts used as conduits for layering.

Alerts on unusual countries, corridors, deposit locations and geolocation dispersion relative to the customer profile or on activity near designated risk regions. It focuses review on geographic anomalies.

Compares the serial payment message with the accompanying cover message so that originator, beneficiary and intermediary details can be checked for consistency. It stops parties being hidden by splitting a payment chain across messages.

ctl.n: Payment message completeness and quality controls
ctl.ds: Rejects or queries payments with missing or meaningless party data, tracks deficiency rates and resubmissions and scorecards senders. It improves transparency of payment chains.

ctl.n: Periodic respondent review and volume monitoring
ctl.ds: Reviews respondent activity against expected volumes, updates expected activity and restricts routing via higher-risk banks. It keeps correspondent risk assessments current after onboarding.

Aggregates cash and other activity by customer, related party, account, branch, channel and day so that splitting across touchpoints cannot evade review, supported by a single customer view. It gives analysts a holistic picture of exposure.
Links accounts, devices, addresses, directors and beneficiaries to surface rings, shared attributes and flow structures that single-account views miss. It supports detection of organised networks.
Traces exposure of deposit and withdrawal addresses to illicit clusters and screens wallets with risk-scored alerts. It reveals on-chain exposure.
Flags direct and indirect exposure to mixers, privacy services and obfuscation tools against defined thresholds and applies enhanced review. It manages the traceability loss these tools create.

ctl.n: Counterparty VASP and platform due diligence
ctl.ds: Assesses the licensing, AML controls, jurisdiction and reputation of counterparty exchanges, over-the-counter desks and other virtual asset service providers before enabling flows, and reviews them periodically. It limits exposure through weak or complicit counterparties.

ctl.n: Country, corridor and port risk rating framework
ctl.ds: Maintains documented risk ratings of countries, corridors, ports and booking centres drawn from transparency, corruption and mutual-evaluation sources, updated on a schedule and after relevant events. The ratings feed due diligence, monitoring and limits.

ctl.n: Funds hold, freeze and recall procedure
ctl.ds: Provides a defined, legally grounded capability to restrict, hold, freeze or recall funds and accounts pending review or on confirmed exposure, with clear triggers and approvers. It stops onward dissipation of suspected illicit funds.
Checks parties against previously filed internal reports, links to reported accounts and feeds report outcomes back into tuning. It spots repeat subjects and sharpens detection.

ctl.n: Correspondent respondent due diligence and risk rating
ctl.ds: Assesses respondent banks' jurisdiction, ownership, regulation, products and AML controls at onboarding using questionnaires and risk rating, including counterparty bank review. It sets the basis for correspondent relationships.

Sends requests for information to respondents or senders with deadlines, tracking of response quality and escalation of repeated deficiencies. It resolves unexplained activity and pressures partners to improve.
